findings.title: Cleanup job ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The background cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This makes all cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, query history) run 10x more often, which is a significant and unrelated behavior/load change — and because each `clean()` run has a 9-minute timeout, runs can now overlap/stack up. This looks like leftover debugging from testing the annotation cleanup and should be reverted.

findings.title: Debug logging left in at Error level, logging full ID lists
findings.body: `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", ..., "ids", ids, ...)` (and the analogous calls at lines 537, 554, 557, 576, 579) log routine, successful cleanup progress at ERROR severity, and include the entire batch of IDs. With a batch size of up to tens of thousands this produces huge log lines every cleanup cycle and will trigger error alerting/noise for operators. These should be removed or downgraded to Debug without dumping the ID slice.

findings.title: SQLite parameter-limit check uses configured batch size instead of actual ID count
findings.body: The decision whether to inline IDs into the DELETE statement is based on `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` rather than `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit`. Also, the limit is applied only for SQLite; other drivers have their own limits (e.g. Postgres allows at most 65535 bind parameters), so a batch size above that would fail at runtime on Postgres. Basing the branch on `len(ids)` and applying a safe limit for all backends (or chunking the deletes) would be more robust.

findings.title: fetchIDs builds SQL by string concatenation of caller-provided condition
findings.body: `fetchIDs` interpolates both the table name and a free-form `condition` string directly into the SQL text, and callers build the condition with `fmt.Sprintf` including `annotationType` and `cutoffDate`. Current callers pass constants/ints so there is no live injection, but this pattern is fragile: any future caller passing user-derived input creates an injection. Parameterizing the cutoff date and keeping the condition to a fixed set of templates would avoid this.
